newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares bouyed over prospects of Iraq deals.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares bouyed over prospects of Iraq deals.

text.p: Jordanian shares rose 0.87 percent on Tuesday with strong demand on blue-chip industrials that might service Iraq after implementation of the U.N. approved oil-for-food deal, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 1.28 points to 148.24 points in healthy trade worth 835,098 dinars ($1,179,516).
"The firms that are related to Iraq such as the vegetable oils and drugs companies saw some activity but there were no stocks that led the market as such," said one broker.

Industrial companies that cater for the Iraqi market appeared to gain ground with investors favourably reacting to news that Iraq and the U.N. had reached an accord on an oil-for-food deal that would permit Baghdad to sell oil in international markets for the first time in six years.
Bouyed sentiment pushed prices higher across the board, with overall rising shares outnumbering fallers by 30 to 5 on Tuesday, with eleven shares trading but closing unchanged.
Most of of the activity was focused on key bluechips with some attention on drug shares and some speculative stock, dealers said.

The market has been anxiously awaiting a trade revival with Baghdad, Jordan's main trade partner and supplier of its full oil needs. Traders see the oil-for-food deal as the first signs of an eventual lifting of the six-year trade blockade on Iraq, which has struck a heavy blow to some of Jordan's industries.
Two chemical firms led the price rises: Intermediate Petrochemicals with a 5.21 percent rise to 1.01 dinars along with Arab Pharmaceutical Chemicals which rose 5.13 percent to 1.23 dinars.
Heavyweight Arab Bank dominated trade with a 1.25 dinar rise to 248.50 dinars with 148,970 dinars worth of shares exchanging hands.

The exchange, worried that trade to the West Bank and sanction-hit Baghdad will remain blocked for the forseeable future, has been stuck around 147 points for the last two months. Turnover has halved to under 500,000 dinars a day.
The Pearl Index of the 45 most prominent shares on the exchange rose 0.74 percent on Tuesday to 79.49 points, still 16.77 percent down on the same day last year.
